newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Interior minister proposed as new Bulgaria premier.
newsitem.headline: Interior minister proposed as new Bulgaria premier.

text.p: Bulgaria's ruling Socialists on Tuesday proposed Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev as prime minister to form a new cabinet to deal with the country's grave economic crisis.
Dobrev's nomination has first to be approved by the Socialists' parliamentary allies and then voted on by parliament, said a party spokeswoman.
After months of criticism of his handling of the economy, Zhan Videnov resigned at a party congress on December 21, sparking a showdown between party hardliners and reformists.

Dobrev, 49, emerged as an outspoken critic of Videnov at the congress, where he attacked the cabinet's record in handling the country's economic and social crisis and raised the previously taboo issue of government corruption.
Dobrev became interior minister in May after his predecessor Lyubomir Nachev was dismissed for failure to deal with escalating crime.
He is now perceived as one of the party's strongmen due to the access to information provided by his post, political analysts say.
If approved, Dobrev will form a new cabinet in the coming days.
Critics of Dobrev's candidature say he lacks the economic background necessary to win the approval of Bulgaria's foreign partners.

Two IMF missions visited Bulgaria in December to help the government and the central bank prepare the introduction of a currency board, proposed to halt the collapse of the national currency and curb inflation.
One of the first tasks of the new government may be to redraft this year's budget, as the budget introduced to parliament by Videnov last week was criticised for unrealistic assumptions.

The opposition has staged protest rallies outside Socialist headquarters in Sofia and other major cities in the past few days, demanding early elections. More rallies are planned in Sofia later in the week.
